metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward in next few days; apply mild upward bias to prevent premature correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping from 48+ to 40+ within 3–5 days), model tends to underestimate the drop; increase downward bias in subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting forecast direction; apply 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment shift.
- In low volatility or consolidation phases, model often overestimates downward trend; reduce forecast slope or add slight upward bias to avoid false bearish signals.
- If true outcome deviates significantly from model’s 30-day average (e.g., >3σ), consider reweighting forecast with sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% model + 30% sentiment-adjusted trend).
